digest.component_or_area: LLM provider seam and runtime abstraction layer
propositions: rebar's LLM runtime is hardcoded to Anthropic-shaped behavior via inline string matching (runner.py:268, runner.py:316, runner.py:653), blocking native Bedrock and generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints despite documented config keys already parsing base_url and api_key.

AWS Bedrock-hosted Claude is not supported despite being a primary access path for clients, and gateway-only approaches forfeit prompt caching, structured output, native retry semantics, and accurate model provenance in signed verdicts.
Documentation claims base_url/api_key composition works (llm-framework.md:126-133,226) but _pai_check_config actively rejects them, creating a false contract.

pydantic-ai 1.107.1 provides a provider_factory hook (infer_model signature) and ModelProfile override injection (BedrockConverseModel.profile parameter) that enable provider abstraction without patching internal functions, but rebar does not use them.
Signed verdict sidecars record a model string that no longer names the actual provider or endpoint when routed through generic gateways, obscuring provenance and tier (first-class vs best-effort).

Two support tiers are required: first-class (Anthropic direct + Bedrock, full fidelity, equivalent retry/timeout guarantees per transport) and best-effort (OpenAI-compatible, one builder, capability losses accepted).
